budget_items.topic: North Cemetery engineering scope of work (Dillis and Roy)
budget_items.what_was_said: The engineering firm's updated survey/design quote for the back lot expansion would be paid out of the cemetery's capital funds. Members said the price compared favorably to other engineering firms' rates.
A member noted the total price for the engineering work, which starts with a wetlands-resources check that determines whether further filing steps are needed.
Members discussed that competitive bidding is normally required above a threshold, but engineering services are exempt from that requirement.
Old quotes from 2023 and 2013 for replacing the front hedge trees were reviewed, covering different tree sizes and counts, as a baseline for updated pricing.
A member sketched rough material costs for a granite/wood post-and-rail alternative to hedging, based on retail pricing.
A New Hampshire granite post specialist quoted a price to set posts along a stretch of frontage, excluding rails, labor and painting.

budget_items.topic: Headstone repair quote (Amanda Construction), South Cemetery front section
budget_items.what_was_said: A stonework/wall contractor quoted repairing tipped, cracked and uneven historic headstones in the oldest section, itemized by type of repair; the full quote exceeds the bidding threshold.
Members recalled a prior, higher hourly-rate quote from another provider for straightening a monument, used for comparison.

budget_items.topic: Hedge trimming quote (Bullock Brothers), North Cemetery
budget_items.what_was_said: A landscaping quote was received to trim and tie back the drooping north-cemetery hedges to prevent snow damage; no competing quote was obtained yet.
A tractor-mounted boom mower service to cut back tree branches overhanging cemetery roads was discussed as either an operational or commission expense, weighed against other planned spending.
Current balances in the sale-of-lots fund and the perpetual-care fund were reviewed as the basis for planning the year's spending, pending confirmation from the town accountant.

budget_items.topic: Interest rate assumption on trust funds
budget_items.what_was_said: An assumed interest rate was used to estimate annual interest income on the two funds, to be verified with the accountant since actual reported interest looked like an unusually high return.

Lot sales over the past five years in the south and north cemeteries were tallied at a flat per-lot price to estimate typical annual revenue, with 2025 sales so far running well below the recent average.

budget_items.topic: Average annual lot sales and revenue estimate
budget_items.what_was_said: Average yearly lot sales for each cemetery were used to project a rough annual revenue figure, which a member cautioned may not hold this year given low year-to-date sales.
Based on interest plus average annual lot-sale revenue, members discussed how much could be spent this year while preserving fund principal, and considered starting conservatively.

budget_items.topic: Capital article transfer carryover and funds currently available
budget_items.what_was_said: A prior capital article transfer left an unspent balance, which combined with perpetual-care interest gives the commission money on hand right now for planned projects.

budget_items.topic: FY spending plan across current projects
budget_items.what_was_said: Members totaled the likely near-term costs (headstone repair, cabinet, contingency) against available funds and decided to hold off drawing further reserves until a November meeting.

budget_items.topic: WB Mason fireproof file cabinet payment
budget_items.what_was_said: The commission approved paying the invoice for a fireproof file cabinet purchased from WB Mason.

minutes.headline: Commission approved an engineering contract for North Cemetery's back-lot expansion and began a fund-spending plan.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Cemetery Commission approved an updated engineering scope of work for the North Cemetery back lot expansion, to be paid from capital funds, and reviewed sale-of-lots and perpetual-care trust fund balances to plan spending on headstone repair, hedge/fence replacement, and road work. No public comment was offered, and the commission approved payment for a file cabinet and scheduled August site visits to both cemeteries.

what_happened.line: The Cemetery Commission approved an engineering firm's scope of work for a North Cemetery back-lot expansion, paid from capital funds.
Members reviewed sale-of-lots and perpetual-care trust fund balances, pending accountant confirmation, to plan the year's spending.
The commission chose to start with a pilot phase of leaning and fallen headstones before deciding on more extensive cracked-stone repairs.
The commission approved payment for a file cabinet and scheduled site visits to both cemeteries for mid- and late August.

why_it_matters: This sets in motion an engineering-funded expansion of North Cemetery and starts committing capital and trust funds to headstone repair, hedge or fence replacement, and road work.

Spending from the perpetual-care and sale-of-lots trust funds is being planned now but was not finalized; the interest-rate assumption behind those fund estimates still needs the town accountant to confirm it.
A legal question about the commission's authority to repair privately owned headstones using perpetual-care funds remains unresolved.
watch_next: November meeting: revisiting whether to pull additional trust-fund money
